Feet in the Sand, Head in the Clouds - 4-Day Itinerary

DAY 1 - SAN JOSE

San Jose should strictly be your port of arrival.

After we toured the National Theatre during the day, we had no choice but to coop up in our Airbnb after sundown. The scenes of people rushing to catch the last buses before sun sets is unsettling.

But you quickly learn why, as the streets are taken over by unsavoury elements. Even restaurants shut down and so we were eternally grateful for Cafe Rojo for staying open until the ungodly hours of 8:30 PM.

DAY 2 - MONTEVERDE

Early next morning, we took the bus from San Jose to Monteverde (about 5 hours away). The roads up the hill are narrow and winding, so be warned if you plan to drive yourself.

On arriving in Monteverde, we immediately felt better about our trip! The place had a wonderful welcoming vibe exemplified by our hostel, Monteverde Backpackers. Filled with travellers from across the world (mainly Europe), it had the communal feeling you want from a hostel.

After dark, we did a night tour of the forest. In a couple of hours, we saw a sloth, a scorpion, a tarantula, a viper, and toucans of various hues. Our guide’s fascinating personality elevated the experience.

DAY 3 - MONTEVERDE

On dia dos in Monteverde, we explored the cloud forests by day with our newfound hostel friends. We took lots of pictures of and on the most famous hanging bridge.

After feasting our eyes on the forest greens, we added a dash of colour by visiting a bird park that housed exotic species.

In the afternoon, it was time for the main event. The mist descending on the hills is a spectacle. One that must experienced for a camera cannot capture the dreamlike atmosphere the clouds create.

The evening was spent back in the hostel, with conversations over cooking.

DAY 4 - MONTEVERDE

Most people who come to Monteverde Cloud Forest, are to experience life as a cloud soaring over the lush valleys.

If you’re scared of heights (as one of us most certainly is), it will be the most terrifying day of your life. Once you cross the first of 13 zip-line cables, there’s no turning back.

But somehow, we did it. And boy was it worth it!

As a famous ad punchline back in India goes, “Darr ke aage jeet hai”. “Beyond fear lies victory”.

For the even more adventurous (which the other of us is), there’s a Tarzan swing where you plunge from a platform into the open sky.

After our nerves had settled, we headed back to other kind of danger, San Jose, to catch our flight out.
